newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures close higher across the board.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures close higher across the board.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher across the board on Friday, reflecting a firmer corn market overnight in Chicago and the yen's weaker tone, traders said.
Prices were 20 to 110 yen higher, with the benchmark May 1998 contract up 20 yen at 15,810 yen per tonne. The day's trade volume was 25,099 lots.
Light buying from local investors emerged from the opening, supporting all contracts, traders said.
But trading was quiet due to Japan's "Golden Week" holidays and because of a reluctance to trade actively before the USDA's crop report is released, they said.
"We're waiting for the USDA's crop report on May 12," a commodity brokerage house trader said.
The Tokyo corn market will be closed on Monday due to a national holiday.
The spot May contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was at $2.98 per bushel at 0755 GMT, down from $2.98-1/2 at Thursday's close.
Spot May CBOT soybean futures were at $8.82 a bushel, up from $8.80-1/4 at Thursday's close.
